summary.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 34% YoY to INR592 crore, with transactions up 36% and GMV up 31%. Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. Loss before tax narrowed to INR13.7 crore from INR18 crore, and management said the emerging share of revenue reached 30%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 18.0% last year; CM amount +43% YoY, +10% QoQ
YoY; gap vs adjusted EBITDA driven by share-based payments

segments.name: Core (shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR412 crore, up 22% YoY; transactions up 31%. Adjusted EBITDA INR52.7 crore at 12.8% margin, up 50 bps YoY. Contribution margin 8.4% vs 8.7% last year.

segments.name: Emerging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 70% YoY and 14% QoQ; now 30% of revenue vs 24% last year. Adjusted EBITDA margin -24% vs -38%; contribution margin about 15% per CEO vs 9% to 10% last year (39.6% vs 47.3% per CFO's company-level breakdown, which is inconsistent).

segments.name: Omnichannel (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 92% YoY, the largest emerging sub-business; driven by quick commerce and PTL (cargo) fulfilment.

segments.name: Cross-border (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue down marginally YoY; management cited global volatility hitting merchant confidence and a focus on higher-margin customers.

segments.name: MarTech (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Youngest and smallest emerging unit, growing very fast at a slightly better margin; checkout (Quikpay), Steal Deal, AI Assist and AI Ads launched this quarter. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance. Management said core contribution margin should stay around its recent trajectory and gave no timeframe for emerging EBITDA break-even.
Core adjusted EBITDA margin has moved from about 6% to 12.8% over three years, but management said it will keep investing behind growth, so no steady-state margin was given.
Management expects Q3 to be the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: Shiprocket owns no logistics assets and works with 42+ courier partners and 250+ partners overall.
Company has about 1,500 employees, with much of the investment going into emerging products and tech.
No capex or capacity figures were discussed.
demand_pricing: Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22%, which management attributed to input cost (courier rate) compression passed on to merchants and mix shift toward larger D2C merchants.
Cross-sell: share of core merchants buying emerging rose to 8.8% from 7.3% a year ago; merchants served via emerging rose to about 48,000 from about 30,000.

Power merchant ARPU rose about 25% while the power merchant count was slightly lower YoY, per the analyst's question; management attributed this to top merchants growing faster and a focus on expanding the funnel.
Blended CAC was about INR3,600 this quarter vs INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management said it is experimental, not seasonal, and that it breaks even within a short period.
Management said pricing is volume-based and that competition in single-point solutions exists, but its data scale is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Will core contribution margin and EBITDA margin keep growing faster than revenue, and is 12.5% to 13% a steady-state core EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CM improved slightly over revenue growth and should stay around that range. It declined to give a steady-state margin, citing continued investment in growth and operating leverage over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeframe was given. Management said MarTech is higher margin and growing fast from a small base, and that growth is the main lever for margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Top merchants are growing faster, and the company is expanding the merchant funnel to convert more merchants into power merchants over time. Management said near-term results depend on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q3 is typically weakest, because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season. No other seasonality was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why has realization per shipment fallen (from about INR96 in FY24 to about INR72 now, per analyst's calculation)?
qa_highlights.answer: The 216 million figure is total unique transactions, not core shipments. Management said the decline reflects the mix shift toward emerging (30% of revenue) and a rise in transactions, while margins as a percentage improved. Core shipment count was not disclosed.

risks_watch: Emerging segment adjusted EBITDA still negative at -24% with no break-even timeframe given; watch whether the margin gap closes as emerging rises toward 30%+ of revenue.
Blended core CAC rose to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management called it experimental and not seasonal, so track whether it stays elevated.
Cross-border revenue fell marginally YoY on global volatility and merchant confidence; check whether this persists into Q2.
Q3 is guided as the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
Emerging contribution margin figures were inconsistent on the call (CEO cited about 15% vs 9-10%; CFO's company-level breakdown showed 39.6% vs 47.3%); clarify the definition before modelling.
Core input cost (courier rate) compression is being passed on to merchants; core revenue growth (22%) trailed transactions (31%), so watch for realization pressure.
key_quotes: The core has been profitable, for quite some time now.
Adjusted EBITDA, although on a very small base, frankly, grew 9x to INR8.9 Crore
Sachin, won't be able to give you a timeframe in terms of guidance, but I think the MarTech business is higher margin, yes, and it's growing at a very rapid clip.
So, quarter 3 tends to be like not the best quarter for our company, unlike the rest of the general e-commerce trends.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, transactions and the rise in contribution margin, and on the emerging trajectory. It was cautious and evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give a steady-state core EBITDA margin or any break-even timeframe for emerging, and it did not disclose the core domestic shipping breakup or core shipment count.
